data.title: NerdWallet expects Q3 revenue of $244M-$260M while scaling IRR-based marketing investment
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: NerdWallet (NRDS) Q2 2026

Management view

  • "We reported revenue of $197 million for the second quarter, up 6% year-over-year" and "Non-GAAP operating income, or NGOI, of $12 million was above the midpoint of our guidance range" (Co-founder, Chairman & CEO Tim Chen).
  • "We're in the middle of an AI transition that is changing how people get their answers to their money questions" and "We're investing in building owned audiences by vertically integrating in some areas and by improving how we register and re-engage with users" (CEO Chen).
  • "The success we are seeing in vertical integration plays across our brokering and advisory business lines is giving us conviction to start investing incremental marketing dollars based on internal rate of return, or IRR, targets rather than solely on in-quarter profitability" and "For the full year 2026, we expect to grow this incremental investment fivefold versus 2025" (CEO Chen).
  • "Consumer revenue was $175 million, up 8% year-over-year" while "SMB revenue was $22 million, down 11% year-over-year" (Chief Financial Officer Jun Lee).
  • "Our trailing 12-month adjusted free cash flow grew 100% year-over-year to $141 million, a new record" and "During the quarter, we repurchased $23 million of Class A common stock" (CFO Lee).

Outlook

  • "We expect to deliver third quarter revenue in the range of $244 million to $260 million" and "we expect non-GAAP operating income in the range of $29 million to $37 million" (CFO Lee).
  • "Our Q3 guidance reflects typical seasonality in our business, as well as expected tailwinds from regulatory changes in student loans and the impact of our College Finance acquisition in February" and "we expect our annual profitability to be more concentrated in the third quarter this year than in prior years" (CFO Lee).
  • "For the full year, we're narrowing our NGOI expectation to a range of $90 million to $105 million, maintaining the midpoint of our previous guidance" and "This guidance includes a $15 million to $20 million NGOI impact from customer acquisition spend with payback periods beyond the current year" (CFO Lee).
  • Analysts’ estimates were provided, but the JSON fiscal quarter format was not consistent with the required Q1-Q4 validation rules, so no estimates comparison is included.

Financial results

  • "Total revenue in Q2 was $197 million, up 6% year-over-year" and "Consumer revenue was $175 million, up 8% year-over-year" (CFO Lee).
  • "This was partially offset by a decline in consumer credit cards, primarily due to continued organic search headwinds" and "Our largest auto insurance carrier relationship has stabilized, but not yet returned to the level seen earlier in the year" (CFO Lee).
  • "Q2 GAAP operating income was $7 million, and NGOI was $12 million at a 6% margin" and "Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $23 million" (CFO Lee).
  • "As of June 30, we had $62 million of cash and cash equivalents" and "we had $67 million remaining under our share repurchase authorization" (CFO Lee).

Q&A

  • Ralph Schackart, William Blair: asked why NerdWallet is increasing investment "fivefold" with "longer payback duration" and requested payback color; Chief Financial Officer Lee responded, "we're beginning to see cohorts of our consumers with high retention and recurring revenue" and described "an LTV to CAC optimization over a longer period of time while using IRR and payback period as guardrails" (CFO Lee).
  • Ralph Schackart, William Blair: asked about "LLM traffic" and "SEO headwinds"; Co-founder, Chairman & CEO Chen answered, "The traffic is converting well" and "It continues to be a pretty small part of our business today, but it's definitely an area of investment and growth for us" (CEO Chen).
  • Michael Infante, Morgan Stanley: asked about distribution value in an AI future and CAC implications; CEO Chen said, "brand and reach are just an incredible asset" and "Brands with higher trust are going to have advantages" as NerdWallet "banking on" vertical integration (CEO Chen).
  • Michael Infante, Morgan Stanley: asked about SMB being "down 11%" and recovery versus prioritizing consumer vertical integration; CEO Chen said SMB has "2 distinct parts," noting "where we're really seeing headwinds year-over-year is on the non-loans part of the business, and loans is growing year-over-year" and added "we're investing in both" channels/CRM and brokering efficiency (CEO Chen).

Sentiment analysis

  • Analysts’ tone was slightly negative to neutral, concentrating on durability of returns and search/AI disruption, including questions on "longer payback duration," "SEO headwinds," and the "path to recovery" in SMB (William Blair; Morgan Stanley).
  • Management tone was slightly positive and investment-focused, emphasizing confidence and positioning, including "we are confident" (Co-founder, Chairman & CEO Tim Chen) and describing IRR discipline as "a capital allocation question" with "a very high bar" (Chief Financial Officer Lee).
  • Versus last quarter’s emphasis on uncertainty from insurance partner monetization, this call’s prepared remarks leaned more toward scaling an IRR-based playbook, while Q&A continued to probe AI/search dynamics.

Quarter-over-quarter comparison

  • Guidance frame shifted from Q1’s "we expect to deliver second quarter revenue in the range of $186 million to $202 million" (CFO Lee, prior call) to Q2’s "third quarter revenue in the range of $244 million to $260 million" and "non-GAAP operating income in the range of $29 million to $37 million" (CFO Lee, current call).
  • Investment language evolved from Q1’s "we've decided to be more aggressive in placing our long-term bets" (CEO Chen, prior call) to Q2’s "conviction to start investing incremental marketing dollars based on" IRR and an expectation to grow that incremental investment "fivefold versus 2025" (CEO Chen, current call).
  • Auto insurance commentary moved from Q1’s warning that monetization from "one of our large partners started running below our expectations" (CEO Chen, prior call) to Q2’s update that the "largest auto insurance carrier relationship has stabilized, but not yet returned" (CFO Lee, current call).

Risks and concerns

  • "Organic search headwinds" remained a stated pressure point, affecting "consumer credit cards" and SMB products (Chief Financial Officer Jun Lee).
  • Concentration and volatility in auto insurance persisted, with management noting stabilization but not recovery in its largest carrier relationship and highlighting a mitigation approach: "scaling with other leading auto insurance carriers and expanding our in-house insurance agency" (CFO Lee).
  • The company acknowledged longer paybacks tied to the new investment approach, stating guidance includes an NGOI impact from "customer acquisition spend with payback periods beyond the current year" (CFO Lee).

Final takeaway

Management emphasized that Q2 results and updated guidance support a shift toward scaling owned-audience strategies and vertical integration through IRR-based marketing investments, while continuing to navigate organic search headwinds and a not-yet-recovered large auto insurance carrier relationship; leadership framed the AI-driven distribution transition as central to its strategy, pointing to strong cash generation and ongoing share repurchases as it funds longer-payback customer acquisition spend.

data.title: Consensus Cloud reaffirms 2026 revenue of $350M-$364M while outlining Healthcare Strategy group and doc.health tuck-in
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Consensus Cloud Solutions (CCSI) Q2 2026

Management View

  • "We had excellent financial results in Q2, continuing our acceleration of total revenue growth with meaningful contributions from each channel of revenue." (CEO & Director R. Turicchi)
  • "We exceeded our revenue objective with corporate revenue posting a 9.3% growth over Q2 2025 ahead of our forecast." (CEO & Director Turicchi)
  • "Free cash flow was $25.5 million in the quarter" and "we were able to repurchase approximately $9.6 million of our stock during the quarter or approximately 300,000 shares." (CEO & Director Turicchi)
  • "The first is the formation of our new Healthcare Strategy and Solutions group headed by Steve Tolle and the second is the tuck-in acquisition of doc.health." (CEO & Director Turicchi)
  • "We will continue to hire into this business unit and its related areas over the balance of the year and into 2027 as we look for meaningful contributions from this group to our non-fax revenue in 2028 and beyond." (CEO & Director Turicchi)
  • "The corporate channel achieved a major milestone, crossing the $60 million mark for the very first time to deliver a record $60.5 million in total revenue for the quarter." (Chief Revenue Officer & Executive VP of Operations Johnny Hecker)
  • "Our NRR continued its upward climb this quarter by more than 1%, reaching 103.1%, up from 102% in Q1." (CRO & EVP Operations Hecker)
  • "Consolidated revenue of $91.4 million represents an increase of $3.6 million or 4.1% over Q2 2025" and "adjusted EPS of $1.49". (Chief Financial Officer Adam Varon)

Outlook

  • No usable analysts-estimates comparison was included because the provided estimates used a nonstandard quarter format that did not match the required Q1-Q4 validation.
  • "We are reaffirming our full year 2026 outlook" of revenue "$350 million to $364 million," adjusted EBITDA "$182 million to $193 million," and adjusted EPS "$5.55 and $5.95." (CFO Varon)
  • "Moving to Q3 2026 guidance. Revenues between $89.2 million and $93.2 million" with adjusted EBITDA "$45 million" to "$48 million" and adjusted EPS "$1.34 to $1.44." (CFO Varon)
  • "Albeit immaterial, we have incorporated our recent doc.health acquisition into our full year guidance" with impact of "revenues approximately $1 million; EBITDA, negative $0.6 million; EPS, negative $0.02." (CFO Varon)
  • "Based on our first half 2026 performance, Q3 2026 guidance range and acquisition impact, we expect full year revenues to be between the midpoint and high end of the range." (CFO Varon)

Financial Results

  • "Consolidated revenue growing 4.1% year-over-year to $91.4 million." (CRO & EVP Operations Hecker)
  • "Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $48.3 million" and "a solid 52.9% EBITDA margin". (CFO Varon)
  • "Free cash flow of $25.5 million" and "We ended Q2 2026 with approximately $99 million in cash". (CFO Varon)
  • "Our Board of Directors has authorized an amendment in our equity repurchase plan to approve an increase in the total authorization to $200 million" and "leaving approximately $118 million available". (CFO Varon)
  • "Our Q2 2026 total debt balance stands at approximately $558 million" and "Our net debt-to-EBITDA ratio for Q2 2026 was 2.45x". (CFO Varon)

Q&A

  • Jenny Shen, BTIG, LLC, Research Division: asked whether hospital spending and vendor scrutiny were changing conversations and why full-year guidance was reaffirmed; CRO Hecker said "hospitals are a little bit -- they're slowing down" and "we're emphasizing ROI," while CEO Turicchi said "it is not our practice" to raise annual ranges after quarterly beats and added the company expects to be "between the midpoint and the high end" on revenue and "outperform the midpoint somewhat" on EBITDA and EPS without changing the range. (CRO Hecker; CEO Turicchi)
  • Isaac Sellhausen, Oppenheimer & Co. Inc., Research Division: asked for more VA ECFax rollout detail and broader public-sector adoption; CRO Hecker said VA sites are "not a number that we publicly announce or publish" and estimated rollout is "somewhere between 65%, 75%, maybe 80%" while noting "active conversations" with contractors, and said other agencies are progressing but "the government still operates at the pace that it does." (CRO Hecker)
  • Isaac Sellhausen, Oppenheimer & Co. Inc., Research Division: asked about hiring and EBITDA margin cadence; CEO Turicchi said headcount is "about 550 employees versus sub-520 when we entered the year" and flagged "an additional $1.3 million of costs" in Q3 tied primarily to audit timing, while stating hires are "primarily in the go-to-market product health care solutions group" and "they're not G&A." (CEO Turicchi)

Sentiment Analysis

  • Slightly negative analyst tone, centered on hospital demand pressure and the decision not to raise guidance: "Have your conversations with hospitals changed at all?" and "What was your decision to reaffirm the full year guide without raising it?" (Jenny Shen, BTIG, LLC, Research Division)
  • Slightly positive management tone in prepared remarks, emphasizing execution and durability, alongside acknowledging buyer friction in health care: "we are pleased to see continued progress" (CRO & EVP Operations Hecker) and "hospitals are a little bit -- they're slowing down" (CRO Hecker).
  • Versus Q1, management kept a consistent guidance posture; Q2 repeated the same principle with CEO Turicchi saying "it is not our practice" to raise the annual range after quarterly beats, aligning with Q1’s "philosophical principle" approach to guidance. (CEO & Director Turicchi)

Quarter-over-quarter Comparison

  • Corporate growth accelerated from Q1’s "8.2%" year-over-year corporate revenue growth to Q2’s "9.3%". (CEO & Director Turicchi)
  • Product and platform messaging progressed from a Q1 "soft launched" rearchitected eFax platform to Q2 "general availability launch of our new eFax platform," plus a Q3 plan for "enhanced mobile capabilities" and an "optional frictionless migration path". (CRO & EVP Operations Hecker)
  • Strategic scope expanded in Q2 with "the formation of our new Healthcare Strategy and Solutions group" and the "tuck-in acquisition of doc.health," while Q1 emphasized the platform as an "AI monetization framework" and hiring catch-up. (CEO & Director Turicchi; CRO & EVP Operations Hecker)
  • Analyst focus shifted from Q1’s guidance philosophy question to Q2 scrutiny on hospital spending, VA rollout, and margin cadence, with management repeatedly pointing to execution pacing and internal cost timing drivers. (CEO & Director Turicchi; CRO Hecker)

Risks and Concerns

  • "Hospitals are a little bit -- they're slowing down" and are "more diligent in their vendor selection" with heightened focus on "EHR integration". (CRO & EVP Operations Hecker)
  • "We fully expect to see volatility in net adds, ARPA and total revenue in the SoHo channel" because management will "not chase low-margin volume". (CRO & EVP Operations Hecker)
  • Margin cadence risk was tied to hiring catch-up and cost timing: "you're starting to see the comp expense ramp" and "the bulk of [audit] fees occur in Q3 and Q4" including "an additional $1.3 million of costs" in Q3. (CEO & Director Turicchi)
  • A non-operating GAAP item was flagged as volatile: "we, on a GAAP basis, booked a $5.3 million gain on an investment" and "these kind of investments are inherently risky" with future valuation changes "up or down". (CEO & Director Turicchi)

Final Takeaway

Management described Q2 as another quarter of corporate-led growth and high margins while keeping full-year ranges unchanged, pairing that posture with a stepped-up healthcare workflow strategy via a new Healthcare Strategy and Solutions group, the doc.health tuck-in, and continued eFax platform rollout. In Q&A, leadership acknowledged slower hospital decision-making and reiterated a guidance philosophy of maintaining annual ranges while positioning full-year results toward the upper portion of the revenue range and slightly above the midpoint for adjusted EBITDA and adjusted EPS, alongside ongoing capital returns through an expanded $200 million repurchase authorization and a continued VA-driven public-sector rollout.

data.title: Millrose Properties commits up to $1.25B to support Dream Finders' Beazer acquisition
data.description:
Millrose Properties (MRP), a homesite option platform, committed to provide financing of up to $1.25B for Dream Finders Homes' (DFH) $2.2B acquisition of Beazer Homes USA (BZH), the company said Friday. It's the third time since Millrose's founding that the company is providing land-banking capital to support a homebuilder acquisition.

Under the agreement, Millrose plans to acquire homesites from the combined Dream Finders (DFH) and Beazer (BZH) organization, allowing Dream Finders to pursue its capital-light strategy. Dream Finders will maintain option agreements on homesites acquired from Beazer, paying option fees during the development period and purchasing finished homesites over time.

Both homebuilders are Millrose clients and have worked with the company through multiple market cycles, Millrose said.

"Builders across the sector are increasingly turning to Millrose for capital-efficient ways to fund growth, preserve balance sheet flexibility, and position themselves for the long term," said Millrose CEO and President Darren Richman.

Millrose Properties (MRP) stock rose 0.7% in premarket trading.

In Dream Finders' (DFH) announcement of the Beazer acquisition, the company said it expects to finance the transaction through a combination of existing capital resources and committed financing from Goldman Sachs (GS), Bank of America (BAC), and affiliates of Kennedy Lewis Asset Management. 

"Following transaction close, Dream Finders expects to continue executing its growth plans while maintaining its commitment to a 100% land-light strategy," the company said.

data.title: Vital Farms reaffirms 2026 guidance and targets ~$775M-$800M net revenue with ~30% gross margin exit run rate
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Vital Farms (VITL) Q2 2026

Management view

  • “While 2026 presented supply dynamics we did not fully anticipate entering the year, we executed decisively to address them, and the early results give us confidence our operational calibration plan is taking hold.” (President, CEO & Executive Chairperson Russell Diez-Canseco)

  • “We believe the second quarter was our financial trough.” (President, CEO & Executive Chairperson Diez-Canseco) “Our net sales declined 10.1%, but the revenue decline and margin compression we were reporting this quarter are consistent with what we told you to expect on our first quarter call.” (President, CEO & Executive Chairperson Diez-Canseco)

  • “As a result, we delivered a more than 200 basis point year-over-year gain in retail dollar share of the shell egg category during the second quarter.” (President, CEO & Executive Chairperson Diez-Canseco)

  • “Since the last earnings call, our price gaps have come down from an average of approximately $2.51 to branded competitors in the first quarter, to an average of $2.36 in the second.” (President, CEO & Executive Chairperson Diez-Canseco) “In the markets where these gaps narrowed, retail volume responded with improved velocity.” (President, CEO & Executive Chairperson Diez-Canseco)

  • “Our farmer contract amendments are now live, and our corporate overhead is structurally lower following difficult but necessary cost realignment actions we took during the quarter.” (President, CEO & Executive Chairperson Diez-Canseco)

  • “Net revenue in the second quarter declined 10.1% to $166 million.” (CFO Thilo Wrede)

  • “We ended the quarter with $21.2 million in cash and had drawn $30 million against our previous revolving credit line.” (CFO Wrede) “After quarter end, we put in place a new $125 million term loan and a new $60 million asset-based lending facility, replacing our previous revolving facility.” (CFO Wrede)

Outlook

  • “We are reaffirming our previous guidance, which calls for net revenue of $775 million to $800 million and adjusted EBITDA of $0 to $10 million.” (CFO Wrede)

  • “We continue to anticipate exiting the fourth quarter at a gross margin run rate of approximately 30%.” (CFO Wrede) “Q3 should mark a sequential improvement in revenue and adjusted EBITDA as breaker volumes abate.” (CFO Wrede)

  • Compared with last quarter’s updated full-year guidance, management reiterated the same ranges: “net revenue of $775 million to $800 million and adjusted EBITDA of $0 million to $10 million.” (CFO Wrede, Q1 2026)

  • The “analystsEstimates” tag was not used because it did not provide a valid fiscal-quarter format consistent with the required Q1–Q4 convention.

Financial results

  • “Gross profit was $10.9 million, or 6.6% of net revenue.” (CFO Wrede) “Gross profit includes a $19.5 million impact from excess breaker sales, $0.8 million from the amortization of farmer contract amendments, and $7.8 million in exit costs associated with our butter wind-down.” (CFO Wrede)

  • “SG&A was $40.4 million.” (CFO Wrede) “This includes $3.3 million of restructuring and severance costs, and $3 million in one-time professional services costs related to our feed cost savings program.” (CFO Wrede)

  • “Adjusted EBITDA was a loss of $26.6 million.” (CFO Wrede) “The loss for the quarter is a result of the peak intensity supply management costs in Q2, totaling $21.8 million for the quarter.” (CFO Wrede)

  • “Full-year supply management costs are now modeled in the mid-$30 million range versus our initial $32 million estimate.” (CFO Wrede) “Importantly, I want to underscore that the contract amendments that are needed for the year are in place.” (CFO Wrede)

  • “At the very beginning of the second quarter, we executed $50 million of share repurchases at an average price of $13.29 per share.” (CFO Wrede) “After the end of the quarter, our board of directors terminated the 2026 stock repurchase plan, consistent with the terms of the new lending facilities.” (CFO Wrede)

Q&A

  • Scott Marks, Jefferies: asked how far the company needs to go on price gaps; President, CEO & Executive Chairperson Diez-Canseco said, “we are right now is very much on track, we believe, to deliver our full year guidance,” and added, “I don't know that on an overall basis for the entire market, we'll get exactly where we want to be this year.”

  • Scott Marks, Jefferies: asked what’s driving distribution wins; President, CEO & Executive Chairperson Diez-Canseco emphasized “the core 4 in existing doors” and highlighted a new item: “we launched a new SKU, which is a 24 count at Whole Foods.”

  • Matthew Smith, Stifel: asked about balancing volume growth vs pricing headwind; President, CEO & Executive Chairperson Diez-Canseco said, “it’s really volume driven from my perspective,” and CFO Wrede pointed to timing, “in fourth quarter, we're dealing with much easier lapping.”

  • Benjamin Mayhew, BMO: asked what the new facilities change; CFO Wrede said the facilities provide flexibility “with $185 million in debt capacity compared to the $60 million that we had before.”

  • Sarang Vora, Telsey: challenged structural margin potential under lower price gaps; CFO Wrede responded, “I don't think we expect anything north of 30,” and said feed savings are intended to “help us pay for the price gap reductions.”

  • Jack Siedow, Needham: asked post-2026 CapEx; CFO Wrede said once through VXR spend, “expect that CapEx spending will fall back down to somewhere of that range,” citing prior “$10 million, $15 million a year.”

Sentiment analysis

  • Analysts’ tone was slightly negative to pressing, concentrating on price-gap depth, structural margin implications, liquidity, and the credibility of the second-half rebound, including “what gives you confidence that swing is going to work.” (Glenn West, William Blair)

  • Management’s tone in prepared remarks was confident and action-oriented, including “we believe our turnaround plan is working,” and in Q&A remained measured on timing and tradeoffs, including “it reflects the right balance of speed, cost, and seeing a return to positive volume growth.” (President, CEO & Executive Chairperson Diez-Canseco)

  • Versus last quarter’s more corrective framing—“fall short of our expectations” and “reset of our expectations for 2026” (President, CEO & Executive Chairperson Diez-Canseco, Q1 2026)—this quarter leaned more toward execution evidence and reaffirmation, including “we are reaffirming our full year guidance today.” (President, CEO & Executive Chairperson Diez-Canseco)

Quarter-over-quarter comparison

  • Q2 emphasized operational proof points—price gap movement to “$2.36,” distribution visibility including “170 to 175 TDPs in the fourth quarter,” and supply actions where “farmer contract amendments are now live.” (President, CEO & Executive Chairperson Diez-Canseco)

  • Q1 centered on diagnosis and a guidance reset, with management saying “price gaps reached levels that our brand could not sustain,” and cutting full-year guidance to “$775 million to $800 million” net revenue and “$0 to $10 million” adjusted EBITDA. (President, CEO & Executive Chairperson Diez-Canseco; CFO Wrede)

  • Financing and capital allocation shifted from Q1’s “no debt outstanding” (CFO Wrede, Q1 2026) to Q2’s post-quarter-end borrowing and constraints, including, “our board of directors terminated the 2026 stock repurchase plan.” (CFO Wrede)

Risks and concerns

  • “2026 presented supply dynamics we did not fully anticipate entering the year.” (President, CEO & Executive Chairperson Diez-Canseco) “We may still see some excess breaker sales in the coming quarters, but at a much reduced level than what we experienced in the second quarter.” (President, CEO & Executive Chairperson Diez-Canseco)

  • “Shipping and distribution expenses increased to 6.4% of net revenue... reflecting the inclusion of $1.5 million of expenses for shipping excess eggs to breaker plants.” (CFO Wrede)

  • “Full-year supply management costs are now modeled in the mid-$30 million range versus our initial $32 million estimate.” (CFO Wrede)

Final takeaway

Management positioned Q2 2026 as the “financial trough,” highlighted narrowing price gaps and expanding distribution as the main drivers for a second-half recovery, and reaffirmed full-year guidance of $775 million to $800 million in net revenue and $0 to $10 million in adjusted EBITDA. The quarter also reflected peak supply-management impacts and a sharp adjusted EBITDA loss, alongside concrete liquidity actions—new debt facilities, a halted repurchase plan, and a controlled CapEx posture—intended to provide runway while supply is rebalanced away from costly breaker volumes.

data.title: Under Armour falls after cutting annual revenue outlook on soft demand
data.description:
Under Armour (UAA) (UA) shares fell about 6% in premarket trading on Friday after the sportswear maker cut its full-year revenue forecast, overshadowing better-than-expected first-quarter adjusted earnings.

The company now expects fiscal 2027 revenue to decline at a mid-single-digit percentage rate, compared with its previous forecast for a slight decline, citing softer demand in North America and Asia-Pacific. It maintained its profitability outlook, including gross margin expansion, operating income of about $106 million, and adjusted diluted EPS of roughly $0.10.

First-quarter revenue for Under Armour (UA) (UAA) fell 3.2% to $1.10 billion, slightly below the Bloomberg consensus of $1.11 billion, while adjusted earnings came in at 5 cents per share, ahead of the 1.8 cent estimate. Adjusted operating income rose to $52.4 million, beating expectations of $36.3 million, while reported operating income was $46.7 million versus the $28.1 million consensus estimate.

Weaker demand remained concentrated in the company's largest market, with North America revenue falling 9%. International sales rose 5%, driven by 12% growth in EMEA, while wholesale revenue slipped 2% and direct-to-consumer sales declined 6%.

"As we navigate a challenging consumer demand environment, we continue to make progress in building a more focused Under Armour, despite updating our full-year revenue outlook," CEO Kevin Plank said.

Shares of UAA rallied about 29% so far this year, outpacing the broader index's 12% gain during the same period. Short interest on Under Armour (UAA) stands at 28.48% of the total float.

data.title: Cloudflare surges as Wall Street praises strong results, guidance
data.description:
Cloudflare (NET) shares surged more than 16% in premarket trading on Friday as several Wall Street firms praised the technology firm for its stronger-than-expected results and guidance.

“The 2Q acceleration, sustained cRPO growth of +34% and broad-based strength across the performance, security and developer platform portfolio point to a business that can sustain 30%+ growth over multiple years and that looks primed to emerge as a preferred infrastructure platform for enterprises and AI-natives to run and orchestrate their agentic workloads, keeping us firmly OW with a $370 PT,” Morgan Stanley analyst Sanjit Singh wrote in a note to clients.

Singh reiterated his Overweight rating on Cloudflare and upped his price target to $370 from $220 after the results.

Bank of America analyst Tal Liani also raised his price target on Cloudflare, as he moved it to $380 from $330, and said the results were a “standout.”

“Cloudflare delivered a standout Q2, with revenue growing 35.9% y/y [vs. the street's] 30.1%, well ahead of expectations and marking another quarter of accelerating growth,” Liani wrote. “The company added a record 282 large customers during the quarter, driving large customer growth to 27% y/y. Dollar-based NRR improved to 120%, up 200bps sequentially and 600bps y/y, while RPO grew 38% y/y. New customer bookings and pipeline generation growth were both highlighted as the strongest they have been in more than five years.”

Jefferies analyst Joseph Gallo said the results and guidance were strong, and Cloudflare is shaking off any worries related to artificial intelligence. “In an environment of ample investor angst about the future of software in an AI world, NET is clearly an AI beneficiary and the company is well-positioned for AI tailwinds and vendor consolidation in cyber,” Gallo wrote.

Gallo has a Hold rating on Cloudflare but upped his price target to $350 from $290.
